area: startup UX: broken gameplay data blamed the --game argument instead of naming the file

find.report_claim: play.py follows the Why:/Fix: convention for every startup failure it handles (old Python, missing Keystone, missing package, import error), so a player always gets an actionable message
find.live_evidence: copying the project, corrupting shooter/data/weapons.json and running play.py produced "Keystone could not start. / Why: Expecting property name ... / Fix: pass a valid package.module:Factory with build_scene, update, ..." -- an actionable message pointing at entirely the wrong thing
find.consumer_evidence: the root cause is on the shooter side: sim._load had no handling for its four REQUIRED data files (weapons, enemies, levels, juice), while the optional engagement.json did have a fallback; keystone's _start_failure_hint then blames the game factory for any load failure because it cannot tell what failed

read: shooter/sim.py _load and the four required loads in Sim.__init__
killed: patching keystone's hint to sniff for file errors: another worker owns that tree, and string-sniffing is worse than the caller knowing its own cause
adding silent fallbacks for the required files: a missing weapons.json means a broken install, and inventing a default would hide it and change gameplay
leaving the traceback: the engine already converts exceptions into Why:/Fix:, so the message was actionable but wrong
analyze.survivor: make the shooter loader raise a ValueError whose message carries Why: and Fix: naming the file and where a good copy comes from; keystone already prints such messages verbatim

fix.shooter: shooter/sim.py _load wraps read_text and json.loads, raising ValueError with the file name, the underlying reason and a restore instruction; tests/test_data_integrity.py (6 tests) covers a missing file, a corrupt file, all four required files being named, the optional engagement.json still falling back to {}, a healthy data dir loading, and the message never containing a traceback

shooter.end_to_end: with weapons.json corrupted, play.py now prints "Keystone could not start. / shooter data file 'weapons.json' is not valid JSON. / Why: Expecting property name ... / Fix: restore <path>/shooter/data/weapons.json from a fresh clone, or repair the JSON at that line."
shooter.mutation: reverting _load to the bare one-liner failed 4 of the 6 tests (missing file, corrupt file, per-file naming, message shape); shooter/sim.py restored byte-identically (sha256 match)
